ivy: Quick note: onboarding ‘marigold7b’ float->int4 conversions. Bench shows top-1 perplexity jump on WebText64 eval only when we apply per-channel asymmetric quant. Other datasets fine. Anyone seen dataset-specific fragility tied to token merges?

mike: Hmm dataset-specific fragility often traces back to tokenization edgecases (URL tokens, punctuation merges). Can you share the token frequency diff between original vocab and converted one for top 1k tokens?

ivy: Uploaded diffs to /tmp/marigold-tokenfreq.csv. Top 10 changed tokens are mostly URL fragments and contractions: e.g., "n't" mapping changed from id 2045 -> 3078; ".com" merge split into "." + "com" in converted version. Eval log excerpt: 
```
webtext64_batch_8: ppl 12.3 -> 18.9 after quant
cc100_batch_8: ppl 15.2 -> 15.6 (small)
openwebtext: ppl 13.1 -> 13.6
```

olga: Two-level hypothesis: token-id shifts cause KV cache warmup mismatches for popular tokens (URLs), and asymmetric quantization shifts projector bias for those frequent tokens. Try symmetric_per_channel and also run a token-remap using frequency-aware matching (map original token ids for top-2k tokens). We have a script: `tools/align_vocab_by_freq.py`.

mike: Also validate rotary freqs and that no headwise scale changed; marigold had a custom rotary base multiplier 1.02 during training. Export step should preserve that. Check `model.rotary.base_mult` present in exported metadata.

ivy: Found base_mult missing in meta.json after conversion. Oops. Recovery plan: re-export meta from float ckpt and re-run quant keeping `rotary.base_mult`. Quick test: quantized + reimported base_mult -> ppl improved from 18.9 -> 14.8 on webtext64. Still worse than float 12.3.

bench-bot: Scheduled regression job: marigold7b-int4-regressions run id 8629990011-1. Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/bench/8629990011

olga: Last mile: do a focused eval where we remap top tokens (URLs, punctuation) to original ids during conversion and preserve rotary base_mult + preserve rotary tables in fp16. That combination tends to restore behavior. Also check embedding projector (proj) quant scale — sometimes per-tensor vs per-channel mismatch there causes bias.

ivy: I'll try frequency-aware remap + rotary fp16 retention and report back. If that fixes, we'll add a converter assertion to copy rotary.base_mult into meta.json.

mike: If you hit a leftover delta, test int4->int8 hybrid (keep embeddings int8, rest int4) as a pragmatic compromise for latency/cost.

ivy: Will do. Thanks folks.
